deviations.what: async failed attempts report no usage: the failed-event payload (FailedPayload, internal/actors/protocol.go) carries no §13.2 Usage field, so a technically-failed async attempt records NULL usage even though the session burned tokens — h24 ('cost includes every attempt') holds only where usage was reportable; sync failures and async completed/blocked are covered
deviations.reason: discovered during t1 implementation: the wire protocol itself only defines Usage on completed/blocked results, not failures — extending it means touching the protocol and all three bridges, past t1's slice; operator adjudicates post-merge per standing instruction

deviations.what: the independent-review pattern cannot bind t10's measured workspace facts: workspace_measured exists only in the Python bridge layer — InvocationResult (internal/actors/protocol.go) has no field for it, and neither binding resolver exposes per-node evidence (/nodes/<id>/evidence is explicitly 'not resolvable yet') — so the example binds the closest honest substitutes (original run input instruction + build node's contract output + the evidence ledger projection) and documents the gap
deviations.reason: discovered during t13: carrying bridge-measured facts to downstream nodes needs a protocol field + binding surface — cross-cutting engine/protocol work outside t13's workflow-pattern scope; operator adjudicates post-merge per standing instruction

deviations.what: per-actor attribution gap found at live verification: attempts.actor_id was only ever set by code nodes — sync agent completions and async callback commits never attributed, so t15's actor stats aggregated nothing for the real fleet; fixed for completed sync+async attempts (DBRegistry.ActorRowID + migration 0015); FAILED attempts remain unattributed (failAttempt's 20 call sites), narrowing per-actor retry-burn until the follow-up lands
deviations.reason: t15's tests inserted actor_id directly in fixtures, so the gap was invisible until the success-signal run hit production topology; failAttempt attribution is a mechanical but broad signature change deferred to keep the closeout fix reviewable
